title: Tidal tightens its AI music rules
summary: Tidal plans to exclude wholly AI-generated tracks, while continuing to allow qualifying AI-assisted music.
body: What Hi-Fi? reports that Tidal’s announced policy takes effect on 9 December. The distinction between fully generated recordings and assisted creative work is central to the change.
takeaway: Uniify perspective: document how your recordings are made, and check your distributor’s current delivery requirements before submitting a release.

title: Independent record shops take the spotlight
summary: Record Store Day’s Black Friday edition brings special releases to independent shops on 27 November.
body: What Hi-Fi? highlights the UK and Ireland’s participating record stores and their limited releases. The event focuses on collecting and discovery rather than a conventional discount sale.
takeaway: Uniify perspective: physical formats can support a closer fan relationship. Check demand and production costs before committing to a pressing.

title: Texas rap reaches more listeners
body: Axios reports increased Texas rap listening, citing Spotify data.
takeaway: Uniify perspective: give your local scene a place in your artist story. Collaborations and shared shows can help listeners discover a connected body of work.

title: Seasonal releases return to the conversation
summary: AP’s holiday music roundup spotlights this year’s seasonal listening and new releases.
body: The Associated Press surveys a range of holiday releases for 2026, including projects from Ashley Cooke and Sufjan Stevens. The coverage shows how seasonal catalogues remain part of the release calendar.
takeaway: Uniify perspective: if a seasonal project fits your music, plan delivery and promotion early rather than rushing to meet a date.

title: TikTok publishes its music discovery report
summary: A TikTok-commissioned Luminate report connects short-form engagement with chart activity and listening.
body: The report says 94% of songs entering the Billboard Global 200 in 2025 had gone viral on TikTok first. It was commissioned by TikTok; the reported association does not establish that posting causes chart success.
takeaway: Uniify perspective: test formats you can sustain and compare engagement with actual listening, rather than treating virality as a release plan.

title: Bandcamp prepares its final Friday of 2026
summary: Bandcamp identifies 4 December as the final revenue-share-waiver event of the year.
body: Bandcamp’s update points artists and fans towards the December event, when the platform waives its revenue share. Check the official event window and applicable payment-processing costs before planning an offer.
takeaway: Uniify perspective: prepare your page, files and fan message ahead of time. Give listeners a clear reason to support a release directly.
